# Test fixtures — provenance and regeneration

Everything under `test/fixtures/` is **generated** (or hand-entered from a cited source) and consumed by
`node --test`. Do not edit generated files by hand; rerun the script named below and commit the result.
The browser app never reads these files and never calls JPL Horizons or IMCCE (NASA CORS policy, JPL fair use).

## `horizons/` — JPL Horizons heliocentric state vectors (`npm run data:horizons`)

Generated by `scripts/fetch-horizons.mjs`. Source: NASA/JPL Horizons API, `https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api`
(API doc: `https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/doc/horizons.html`; planetary ephemeris **DE441** for every body — see the
`targetLine` / `centerLine` fields, which are the verbatim `{source: …}` header lines).

### Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<body>.json` | `{body, command, url, apiVersion, fetchedAt, targetLine, centerLine, frameLine, unitsLine, rows}`; `rows[i] = {jdTT, calendar, x, y, z, vx, vy, vz}` — position in **AU**, velocity in **AU/day**, heliocentric, "Ecliptic of J2000.0" (ICRF x-axis, IAU76 obliquity 84381.448″), geometric (no light-time, no aberration). Rows are sorted by `jdTT` (Horizons sorts a `TLIST`). |
| `<body>.raw.txt` | The verbatim Horizons text response the JSON was parsed from (header, `$$SOE…$$EOE` block, footnotes). |
| `mars-stationary-2024.json` | Derived Mars stationary dates (see below) plus the daily longitude table it came from. |
| `mars-stationary-2024.raw.txt` | Verbatim OBSERVER response. |
| `residuals.md` | VSOP87A (shipped truncated data, scene frame) − Horizons residuals for every body and epoch: km, arcsec (atan2 form), AU/d, with per-band maxima and their 1.3× values. Generated by `node scripts/ephem.mjs --residuals`; the tolerances in `test/horizons.test.mjs` are max(plan, 1.3× these maxima). |

Bodies and Horizons `COMMAND` ids (`mercury 199`, `venus 299`, `earth 399` = planet centres; `mars 4`, `jupiter 5`,
`saturn 6`, `uranus 7`, `neptune 8` = system barycentres). Barycentres are used for Mars–Neptune because Horizons
`499` (mar099) has no data before 1600-01-01 TT, `499` vs `4` differ by 6.4e-14 AU (≈ 1 cm) at J2000, and VSOP87's
outer-planet series represent the barycentres (research bsiou1mfc caveat 4; centre − barycentre for Neptune ≈ 123 km).

### Exact request parameters (VECTORS)

```
format=text  COMMAND='<id>'  OBJ_DATA='NO'  MAKE_EPHEM='YES'  EPHEM_TYPE='VECTORS'  CENTER='500@10'
REF_PLANE='ECLIPTIC'  REF_SYSTEM='ICRF'  OUT_UNITS='AU-D'  VEC_TABLE='2'  VEC_CORR='NONE'  CSV_FORMAT='YES'
VEC_LABELS='NO'  TLIST_TYPE='JD'  TIME_TYPE='TT'  TLIST='<53 space-separated JDs>'
```

Values are single-quoted; the URL is built with `URLSearchParams` (`'` → `%27`, `@` → `%40`, space → `+`) and
stored verbatim in each JSON's `url`. `START_TIME/STOP_TIME/STEP_SIZE` are never combined with `TLIST`.
`TIME_TYPE='TT'` is accepted for vector tables although the doc lists only TDB/UT; the JD column is labelled `JDTT`
and Horizons notes that TT is converted from its internal TDB with |TT − TDB| < 2 ms (< 0.05 km for Mars).

### Epochs (53, JD TT, identical for every body)

- 41-epoch grid **JD 2415020.0 + k · 1826.25, k = 0…40** (1900 → 2100 every 5 Julian years; k = 20 is J2000 =
  2451545.0 exactly). These are the epochs on which the VSOP87 truncation bounds are measured (`vsop87-chk.json`).
- Jan 1 12:00 TT (proleptic Gregorian, Meeus ch. 7) of **1600, 1700, 1800, 1850, 2200, 2300, 2400, 2500, 2600**:
  2305448.0, 2341973.0, 2378497.0, 2396759.0, 2524594.0, 2561118.0, 2597642.0, 2634167.0, 2670691.0.
- **2440000.5** (1968-05-24 0h), **2460000.5** (2023-02-25 0h), **2461297.0** (2026-09-13 12h TT) — the research
  proof-of-concept and sub-solar-fixture epochs.

The script asserts, per response: `API VERSION`, `Center body name: Sun (10)`, `Reference frame : Ecliptic of J2000.0`,
`Output units    : AU-D`, `$$SOE`/`$$EOE`, exactly 53 rows whose JDs equal the requested list in order, and three
reference rows to **1e-12 AU** (values quoted from the planning research's live run): Mars/4 J2000
`(1.390715921745722, −0.01341631816512547, −0.03446766277610819)`, Earth/399 J2000
`(−0.1771350992582233, 0.9672416867691899, −4.085281582660778e-6)`, Neptune/8 J2000
`(16.81204696805071, −24.99176288928619, 0.1272228799203305)`. It also checks that every request started ≥ 1.5 s
after the previous one finished.

### `mars-stationary-2024.json` (experimental stationary-point class)

Source request: `COMMAND='499'  CENTER='500@399'  EPHEM_TYPE='OBSERVER'  QUANTITIES='31'  START_TIME='2024-10-01'
STOP_TIME='2025-04-01'  STEP_SIZE='1d'  CSV_FORMAT='YES'  ANG_FORMAT='DEG'  TIME_TYPE='UT'` (plus `format=text`,
`OBJ_DATA='NO'`, `MAKE_EPHEM='YES'`). Quantity 31 = `ObsEcLon`/`ObsEcLat`: geocentric **apparent** ecliptic-**of-date**
longitude/latitude (light-time + aberration), degrees. Method: daily finite differences of `ObsEcLon` (wrapped to
(−180°, 180°]) attributed to interval midpoints; a sign change between consecutive differences is a stationary point,
located by linear interpolation (+ → − retrograde start, − → + retrograde end). Result: `dates = ["2024-12-06",
"2025-02-24"]` (instants 2024-12-06T23:31 and 2025-02-24T02:02 UT). Geometric J2000 timings differ from these
apparent of-date timings by well under a day; the events test uses ±1 d.

### Fair use / regeneration

`npm run data:horizons` performs exactly 9 GET requests (8 VECTORS + 1 OBSERVER), strictly sequentially, ≥ 1.5 s apart,
with exponential backoff 5 / 20 / 60 s on an HTTP error, network error or a response that fails validation (Horizons
reports its own errors inside a 200 response without `$$SOE`), then aborts. Regenerate only when the epoch list or
parameters change; `fetchedAt` and `url` are refreshed every run, the numbers only change if JPL changes DE441-based
Horizons output. VSOP87-vs-Horizons residual tables (`horizons/residuals.md`) are produced by
`node scripts/ephem.mjs --residuals` and asserted by `test/horizons.test.mjs`, not by the fetch script.

Horizons quirks observed while generating (2026-09-13, API version 1.2):

- `TLIST` rows come back sorted chronologically regardless of request order; `Start time`/`Stop time` in the header
  are the min/max of the list and `Step-size : DISCRETE TIME-LIST`.
- Every VECTORS response was exactly 15,729 bytes: fixed-width CSV (`%.15E`), trailing comma on every row.
- `Calendar mode : Mixed Julian/Gregorian` is printed, but all epochs are after 1582-10-15 so the calendar labels
  (`A.D. 1600-Jan-01 12:00:00.0000`) agree with the proleptic-Gregorian JD routine; keying is by JD only.
- The OBSERVER CSV row is ` YYYY-Mon-DD HH:MM, <solar presence>, <lunar presence>, ObsEcLon, ObsEcLat,`; the two
  presence columns are blank for a geocentric observer but may contain marker letters otherwise — the parser reads
  the two numeric fields from the end of the row.
- `Output format   : 2 (position and velocity)` — VEC_TABLE='2' has no uncertainties or range columns.
